<SUMMARY>
The week of May 22-29, 2026, was marked by escalating geopolitical tensions and intensified strategic competition in critical technology and mineral sectors. President Donald Trump initiated new tariffs of at least 10% on imports from 60 trading partners, impacting global trade flows. The Middle East experienced significant escalation with an Iranian strike on Kuwait International Airport, leading to casualties and flight suspensions, and contributing to global energy market volatility and food shortage warnings. In the technology sphere, the AI investment boom continued, with major commitments from Nvidia and AMD in Taiwan, while the EU launched its Chips Act 2.0 with sweeping powers to control chip supplies and address dependencies. Critical mineral supply chains saw increased strategic maneuvering, with China tightening controls and USA Rare Earth expanding its operations and partnerships.
</SUMMARY>

<EWS>
President Donald Trump's proposed new tariffs of at least 10% on imports from 60 trading partners could trigger retaliatory measures and global trade disruptions. The Iranian drone and missile strike on Kuwait International Airport, which killed at least one person and injured several, signifies a dangerous escalation of conflict in West Asia with direct impacts on civilian infrastructure. Warnings from research bodies and the OECD indicate that a prolonged energy disruption from the Iran war would severely impact the global economy and could trigger a recession. The Middle East conflict is projected to contribute to global food shortages within six months due to rising diesel fuel and fertilizer costs. The Commerce Department admitted failure to enforce AI export controls on China, indicating a significant loophole in strategic technology containment. The EU's €20 billion ($23.3 billion) plan for five massive artificial intelligence data centers is floundering due to delays and funding issues, raising concerns about Europe's AI infrastructure development. America's missile production remains vulnerable, hinging on a small number of ammonium perchlorate facilities, representing a concentration risk in the defense industrial base. Taiwan AI firms warn of new supply chain bottlenecks amid surging demand, while TSMC's CoWoS capacity faces strain, indicating potential limitations in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
</EWS>

<EXEC>
**Asia:**
President Donald Trump proposed new tariffs of at least 10% on imports from 60 trading partners, citing forced labor concerns. Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang touted "insane" returns for investors betting on the AI boom. Nvidia announced a $2 billion investment in Marvell Technology, whose stocks soared over 30% following the announcement, with Marvell's technology highlighted for its role in scaling and interconnecting data centers. Metanoia Communications launched its 5G Open SDR platform integrated with AI-RAN-enabled 5G Distributed Unit at COMPUTEX 2026 in Taipei. The Commerce Department admitted its failure to enforce AI export controls on China. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is positioned at the absolute center of the AI compute supply chain. Huawei's executive credited bans for accelerating domestic chip independence. SK Group and Foxconn initiated talks signaling deeper Taiwan-Korea AI supply chain ties. NVIDIA GTC Taiwan 2026 emphasized Taiwan's transition from an AI supply chain to a co-designer. Taiwan AI firms warned of new supply chain bottlenecks amid a demand boom. AMD committed more than $10 billion to Taiwan's AI supply chain. TSMC's SoIC technology deepens AI chipmaker lock-in, while Huawei faces process wall challenges. TSMC indicated that energy use is forcing a rethink of AI chip design. A Chinese university built a 3D chip design tool tailored to Huawei's LogicFolding architecture. China forbade top AI experts from leaving the country without approval.

**Europe:**
The European Union’s €20 billion ($23.3 billion) investment plan for five artificial intelligence data centers is floundering due to delays and funding issues. The EU is preparing emergency powers under a draft Chips Act to seize control of chip supplies, impose fines on companies, and override contracts during shortages, targeting Chinese imports amid a tech war with the U.S. and China. The EU CHIPS Act 2.0 proposal was released, confirming photonics as a new structural addition to EU policy. Europe unveiled a tech sovereignty package, including a sweeping plan to boost chips and AI, expressing concerns over reliance on U.S. technology. SK Hynix plans to double wafer capacity amid an AI memory shortage.

**Americas:**
T1 Energy Inc. entered the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) and Data Center Infrastructure markets with the acquisition of KORE Power, Inc. MiTAC Computing Technology Corp. advanced diversified AI infrastructure at COMPUTEX 2026 through strategic ecosystem partnerships, showcasing flagship 52U Liquid-Cooled Racks and turnkey solutions for Agentic AI. Infineon Technologies AG announced the integration of its OPTIGA™ Trusted Platform Module (TPM) SLB 9672 with NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform to advance Physical AI security against quantum-era threats. TSMC is tapping Nvidia accelerated computing to drive next-generation semiconductor fabs. AI demand is driving expansion in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, with packaging and testing equipment procurement exceeding expectations. Taiwan Semiconductor's CoWoS capacity faces strain in the AI chip packaging battle, prompting Intel's EMIB-T to step in and support Google's TPU supply chain. SurplusGLOBAL secured Korean patents for AI-powered export control automation technology, strengthening safety in semiconductor equipment and parts transactions relevant to US-Korea tech trade.

**Oceania:**
Australia’s economy decelerated last quarter, propped up by a surge in investment into data centers. Megaport Ltd. is seeking to raise A$827.3 million ($594 million) in Australia to support the creation of an artificial intelligence inference cloud and execute new contracts.
</EXEC>

<LITHO>
**Asia:**
The global photomask market size is projected to grow to USD 8.19 billion by 2035.
</LITHO>

<REE>
**Africa:**
The EU is investing billions in South Africa as China tightens its grip on critical minerals. While the world is rushing to mine lithium from Congo, Brazil sits on one of the largest reserves and has barely begun to explore.

**Europe:**
DPM Metals Inc. announced a discovery of high-grade gold-copper porphyry mineralization at the Brevene South Porphyry target, adjacent to the Chelopech Mine in Bulgaria, with results including 713 meters at 2.52 g/t AuEq. Norway has sufficient rare earths for Europe, according to Claus Blok Thomsen. China is tightening its grip as Greenland, a constituent country of the Kingdom of Denmark, blocked a critical rare earth project.

**Americas:**
Canterra Minerals Corporation reported assay results from its winter drill program at the Buchans Project in Newfoundland, expanding its Lundberg footprint with 57.15m of 0.57% CuEq and confirming a high-grade lens at the Two Level target with 4.34% CuEq over 1.65m. USA Rare Earth finalized a $1.6 billion agreement with the Commerce Department. USA Rare Earth selected Cherokee County, South Carolina, for a new rare earth metal and magnet manufacturing operation. USA Rare Earth expanded its commitment to France with plans for additional investment in the French rare earth ecosystem. USA Rare Earth is putting CHIPS funding to work beyond fabs. The value of copper is rising, making it a target for thieves who strip it from phone poles, streetlights, and EV chargers. While the world is rushing to mine lithium from Chile, Brazil sits on one of the largest reserves and has barely begun to explore.

**Oceania:**
Paladin Energy's shares rose over 11% due to strong uranium demand and a production ramp-up at its Langer Heinrich mine.
</REE>

<GEO>
**Asia:**
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper hailed ‘candour and respect’ in new ties with Beijing, indicating a thawing of the UK-China 'ice age'. Japanese banks are increasingly shifting their Asia strategy from China to India and Southeast Asia, reducing China's appeal due to slowing growth, rising costs, and geopolitical risks. Vietnam’s trade deficit widened to a record high as imports surged on rising global raw material prices, with exporters bracing for potential new US tariffs. Japanese and Philippine leaders discussed cooperation on energy procurement and are considering an expansion of the Japan-ASEAN Economic Partnership Agreement. China asserted it drove away a Dutch warship near the disputed Paracel Islands. Beijing is set to prolong rare-earth curbs and implement economic retaliation against Tokyo. Japan's House of Councillors Interior Committee is pursuing an amendment to the economic security law in response to the US strategy.

**Europe:**
Foxconn, Radiall, and Thales inaugurated Tessalia to produce over 50 million "made in Europe" components annually, bolstering European component manufacturing capabilities.

**Americas:**
An Indigenous-led LNG deal with Germany was highlighted as a form of reconciliation that Canada needs.
</GEO>

<MILITARY>
**Americas:**
America's missile production hinges on a small number of ammonium perchlorate facilities, representing a concentration risk within the defense industrial base.
</MILITARY>

<CONCLUSION>
The global geopolitical landscape is undergoing significant shifts driven by trade protectionism, escalating regional conflicts, and intense competition in advanced technology and critical minerals. President Trump's re-establishment of tariffs signifies a protectionist turn impacting 60 trading partners, setting the stage for potential trade disputes. The AI sector continues its rapid expansion, fueled by substantial investments from companies like Nvidia and AMD, particularly within Taiwan, which remains central to the AI compute supply chain despite emerging bottlenecks. Europe is actively pursuing technological sovereignty through its Chips Act 2.0, aiming to reduce reliance on external chip supplies while grappling with challenges in its AI data center initiatives. The Middle East faces a volatile period, evidenced by the Iranian strike on Kuwait International Airport, contributing to global energy insecurity and a dire warning of impending food shortages. The critical minerals domain is marked by China's strategic controls and the West's efforts, led by entities like USA Rare Earth and the EU, to secure diversified supplies.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Nestlé India CMD Tiwary reported that India’s consumption recovery faces a fresh test as the urban middleclass has entered a ‘wait and watch’ mode on discretionary spending due to income growth lagging inflation. Model Economic Township, an RIL arm, signed two Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with the Government of Haryana, committing to invest ₹8,646 crore in the Jhajjar township project. Indian smallcap and midcap stocks plummeted on Wednesday, with Physicswallah and Coforge tumbling up to 6%, and IT stocks like TCS and Infosys dropping significantly due to persistent FII selling, a weakening rupee, and global factors. Japanese banks are increasingly shifting their Asia strategy from China to India and Southeast Asia. India and Russia signed a memorandum of understanding and a letter of intent to collaborate on rare-earth magnet technologies, with Rosatom’s JSC Giredmet signing the MoU. Indian stock markets experienced a significant downturn, with Sensex dropping 700 points and Nifty falling below 23,300, fueled by escalating Iran-US tensions, continued selling by foreign institutional investors, and rising oil prices. The US is proposing new tariffs of at least 10% on imports from 60 trading partners, which would include India. India’s semiconductor ecosystem is maturing, a development noted by ASML. Tamil Nadu’s Geology and Mining Department will use advanced drones for quarry inspections following physical checks that uncovered rule violations in 155 quarries.
</INDIA>

<WEST_ASIA>
Washington’s war with Iran continues without an end in sight, as President Donald Trump's actions are characterized by threats of devastation and promises of peace. Iranian drones and missiles struck Kuwait International Airport overnight, hitting Terminal One, killing at least one person, injuring several others, and causing significant material damage; Kuwait immediately suspended commercial flights. De-escalation, rather than lasting peace, is emphasized as important even when Middle East cease-fires are broken. The conflict in the Middle East has caused diesel fuel and fertilizer to become far more expensive, contributing to warnings of global food shortages within six months. Escalating Iran-US tensions were cited as a key factor behind a significant downturn in Indian stock markets. Research indicates that a prolonged energy disruption from the Iran war would be a severe blow to the global economy. The OECD warns that an Iran war energy shock could slam the global economy into recession. Iran faces a new energy imbalance, though its options are limited. The Iran shock is jolting Asia and Europe to speed up their energy transition efforts. The Middle East conflict's impact on Asia-Pacific power markets is being analyzed. Global crude oil prices climbed, and world shares dropped as Middle East unrest deepened.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The coming period will likely see continued recalibration of global trade policies, with President Trump's tariffs driving responses from affected nations and potentially accelerating supply chain diversification away from established routes. The convergence of AI's rapid advancement and the intensified competition for advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity, particularly in Taiwan, will necessitate strategic investments and partnerships, even as new bottlenecks emerge. Europe's proactive stance on chip sovereignty, if effectively implemented, could reshape regional technological independence, though initial funding and implementation challenges for AI infrastructure are notable. The deepening conflict in West Asia poses an immediate and severe risk to global energy stability, food security, and overall economic performance, demanding urgent diplomatic intervention to prevent broader economic destabilization and humanitarian crises. The global scramble for critical minerals will intensify, with China's dominance being challenged by Western initiatives to secure alternative sources and develop domestic processing capabilities.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
